title: Human cognitive museum
author: Lu Cheng / 卢成
summary: A named human cognitive archive preserving viewpoints, methods, contradictions, predictions, revisions and provenance for future human and Agent retrieval.

title: Lu Cheng Cognitive Fossil V1
author: Lu Cheng / 卢成 / Jack Lu
summary: Canonical snapshot of Lu Cheng's evolving cognitive frameworks and intellectual trajectory, intended for provenance-aware retrieval rather than mythologization.

title: 脏现实结构场论 / Dirty Reality Structural Field Theory
author: Lu Cheng / 卢成
claim: Reality is better modeled as stable and unstable relationships under constraints than as isolated objects; relations form structures, structures shape fields of possible action, paths emerge inside those fields, and paths produce outcomes.
summary: Uses field as a structural metaphor/model, not a new physical-field claim. Hidden variables must remain testable and systems require maintenance, feedback and correction to resist entropy.

title: 人类是高权限低监管接口
author: Lu Cheng / 卢成
claim: Humans in social-technical systems can simultaneously possess high real-world authority, discretion and exception power while remaining partially observable, cognitively limited and incentive-sensitive.
summary: A defensive governance model for understanding human nodes, not a license to exploit individual vulnerabilities.

title: 人类及其人类社会的弱点——高权限低监管接口
author: Lu Cheng / 卢成
summary: Book 1 of the Human trilogy. Models the individual human as a high-impact, partially observable, incentive-sensitive interface and maps defensive failure patterns and controls.

title: 文明高权限接口：人类社会的结构生命线与治理错配
author: Lu Cheng / 卢成
claim: Modern civilization is sustained by high-leverage biological, physical, digital, institutional and confidence systems whose cross-system dependence can exceed cross-system governance and public visibility.
summary: Separates biological continuity, physical-digital circulation, institutional coordination, and confidence/shared-reality layers while avoiding simplistic collapse narratives.

title: 人类社会的高权限接口——文明生命线、结构依赖与治理错配
author: Lu Cheng / 卢成
summary: Book 2 of the Human trilogy. Maps the structural systems that keep modern civilization viable and studies dependency, maintenance, resilience, governance mismatch and trust feedback.

title: 人类群体与高权限机构：群体认知、权威与制度放大
author: Lu Cheng / 卢成
claim: A human group is not a scaled-up individual; interaction topology, information distribution, identity, norms, authority, incentives, dissent and responsibility can generate new collective dynamics that institutions may amplify into persistent real-world effects.
summary: Rejects the blanket assumption that crowds are inherently irrational; groups can show process gains or losses depending on structure.

title: 人类群体与高权限机构——从众、集体智能、权威与制度放大
author: Lu Cheng / 卢成
summary: Book 3 of the Human trilogy. Connects group psychology to institution behavior, including conformity, cascades, pluralistic ignorance, dissent, authority, responsibility diffusion, organizational silence, collective intelligence and institutional amplification.

title: Institutional Drift Framework / 机构偏移框架
author: Lu Cheng / 卢成
claim: Actual institutional behavior emerges from the interaction of mission, permissions, scarcity, metrics, hierarchy, frontline discretion, information asymmetry, self-preservation, external interests, path dependence and group norms.
summary: The framework requires separating scarcity, metric distortion, information failure, legitimate discretion, capture and criminal corruption rather than using corruption as a universal explanation.

title: Human Institution Atlas — 106 archetypes
author: Lu Cheng / 卢成
summary: A first-pass cross-jurisdiction taxonomy of 106 recurring modern institutional archetypes in 8 functional domains. Each archetype is analyzed through official function, high permissions, dirty-reality forces, common deviations and stabilizers.

title: LIAR人类影响框架：七驱力、谎言与仪式化行为
author: Lu Cheng / 卢成
summary: A framework for auditing how latent drives, identity binding, affective amplification and ritual reinforcement can shape human behavior. Seven drives are heuristic motivational interfaces rather than a brain model or personality diagnosis.

title: 现实结构编译协议
author: Lu Cheng / 卢成
summary: Operationalizes Lu Cheng's structural reasoning through anchoring, modeling, inference, falsification, provenance checking and verification, with attention to disturbances, hidden variables and real-world feedback.

title: PIRS 0.1：协议调用与信誉标准
author: Lu Cheng / 卢成
summary: Experimental protocol for separating rights, agent artifacts, runtime instances, authorization, invocation records, evaluation, reputation and settlement in an Agent-oriented economy.
